title: AboutMe: Using Self-Descriptions in Webpages to Document the Effects of English Pretraining Data Filters

bias_targets.methodology: Geoparsing self-described locations from webpage 'About' sections and comparing the retention, removal rates, and filter scores of websites across different continental regions, subregions, and 'anglophone' statuses when subjected to LLM quality and language identification filters.

Extracting self-identified social roles and occupations from webpages, mapping them to O*NET salary estimates and occupational prestige ratings, and calculating the correlation between these socioeconomic indicators and the scores assigned by model-based quality filters.

Clustering webpages into 50 distinct topical domains based on text embeddings of 'About' pages, and analyzing how different pretraining data filters disproportionately penalize or favor specific topical interests (e.g., news/media vs. fashion/photography).
Training a classifier to categorize websites as belonging to individuals versus organizations, and comparing the average filter scores and exclusion rates between the two groups.
